title: U.S. House · California's 7th District
area: Covers part of the city of Sacramento, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

Because California uses a top-two primary regardless of party, both general-election candidates are Democrats. In the June 2, 2026 primary, challenger Mai Vang placed first with 31.2% (65,617 votes), ahead of incumbent Doris Matsui's 29.1% (61,114 votes), out of 210,115 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: Doris Matsui
candidates.ballotNote: Placed second, behind challenger Mai Vang, in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

summary.text: Doris Matsui is the Democratic incumbent for California's 7th Congressional District. Born in the Poston, Arizona internment camp, she worked in the Clinton White House before winning a 2005 special election to succeed her late husband, Rep. Bob Matsui. She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

background.text: Born Doris Okada in the Poston, Arizona internment camp in 1944, and grew up in Dinuba in California's Central Valley.
Earned a B.A. from the University of California, Berkeley in 1966 (a psychology degree, according to Wikipedia); she met her husband, Bob Matsui, while at Berkeley.

Volunteered on Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential campaign and served on the Clinton-Gore transition team, then worked in the White House Office of Public Liaison from 1993 to 1998, including as deputy director.

President Clinton appointed her to the board of the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars in 2000. Wikipedia reports she then worked as a Washington lobbyist for corporate clients until 2005.

Her husband, Rep. Bob Matsui, died on January 1, 2005. She won the March 8, 2005 special election to succeed him in what was then California's 5th District and has been re-elected since 2006; the district number changed to the 6th in 2013 and the 7th in 2023.

Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including its Communications and Technology and Energy subcommittees (2025-2026); she was ranking member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee in 2023-2024.
Chaired the Democratic Women's Working Group from 2015 to 2017.
Has served on the Smithsonian Board of Regents and as chairwoman of the board of public television station KVIE.
Married AES Corporation co-founder Roger Sant in 2020, according to Wikipedia; she has one son.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists economic investment in manufacturing, clean energy and infrastructure; healthcare policy including the Affordable Care Act and telehealth; flood protection for the Sacramento region; and support for seniors' Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid benefits among her legislative priorities.

positions.summary: Describes herself as a leader on establishing and improving the Affordable Care Act and expanding telehealth access.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Matsui has been a leader in Congress on a broad range of health care issues, from establishing and improving the Affordable Care Act, to reforming mental health and substance abuse care, to expanding the use of telehealth.

positions.summary: Co-chairs the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition and says she has made bringing clean-energy technology to Sacramento a top priority.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Communications and Technology and Energy subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.
Served as Ranking Member of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology during the 2023-2024 session.

candidates.name: Mai Vang
candidates.ballotNote: Placed first, ahead of incumbent Doris Matsui, in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

summary.text: Mai Vang is a Sacramento City Council member for District 8 and the daughter of Hmong refugees from Laos. A former school board member, city council staffer and nonprofit director, she was first elected to the council in 2020 and finished first in the June 2026 top-two primary. She is challenging fellow Democrat Doris Matsui.

background.text: According to the City of Sacramento, Vang is the daughter of Hmong refugees from Laos, a Sacramento native, and the eldest of 16 children.
Holds bachelor's degrees in biology and sociology from the University of San Francisco and master's degrees in public health and Asian American studies from UCLA.
Worked as a community organizer on health and educational outcomes for children and families in south Sacramento, and co-founded Hmong Innovating Politics (HIP), a civic engagement organization.

Served as Community Affairs Director for Sacramento Councilmember Larry Carr at City Hall from 2014 to 2018, and as executive director of the Buck Scholars Association, which provides mentorship and scholarships to high school students.
Served on the Sacramento City Unified School District board (Area 5) from 2016 to 2020.
Elected in November 2020 to the Sacramento City Council representing District 8 (South Sacramento); her term runs through 2028.

Her council office's biography lists first-term work including the Measure L Sacramento Children's Fund ballot initiative, a Food Justice Task Force, and a city purchase of 102 acres in South Sacramento for future development; the Sacramento Bee named her a top AAPI Change Maker in 2022.
Teaches in the Department of Ethnic Studies at California State University, Sacramento, and has taught Asian American Studies at UC Davis; lives in the Meadowview neighborhood of South Sacramento.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

record.text: Elected to the Sacramento City Council, District 8, in 2020, after serving on the Sacramento City Unified School District board from 2016 to 2020.

researchNotes: Mai Vang has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no policy-specific content from her campaign website could be retrieved during research, so her stated priorities and positions could not be documented beyond her prior officeholder record. Biography gaps: the Matsui House site directs readers to her office for an official biography and Bioguide blocked fetching, so her early life, White House and lobbying details rest on Wikipedia; no personal details for Vang beyond her council office's biography were found.
